title: Career roadmap · Financial Planner
summary: A Financial Planner helps individuals or organisations make informed decisions about investments, savings, insurance, retirement, taxation and long-term financial goals.

facts.Timeline assumption: This roadmap assumes a standard 3-year B.Com. If your university offers a 4-year honours/research variant, use the additional year for advanced investment analysis, financial-planning projects, internships and professional certifications.

about.label: Course alignment
about.text: Financial Planner is directly aligned with the B.Com – Investment / Wealth Management pathway.

horizons.question: What can I enter now?
horizons.output: Build accounting, economics, investments, taxation, insurance, Excel and financial-planning fundamentals; complete internships and begin relevant NISM/CFA/financial-planning preparation.

horizons.question: How should I specialise?
horizons.output: Specialise in personal financial planning, wealth management, investment advisory, retirement planning, portfolio analysis or HNI/UHNI client services.

horizons.question: How should I evolve?
horizons.output: Progress toward Senior Financial Planner, Wealth Manager, Investment Advisor, Relationship Manager or Financial Planning Lead responsibilities.

horizons.question: How can I remain relevant?
horizons.output: Combine investment expertise with financial technology, behavioural finance, tax awareness, AI-assisted analysis, client relationships and strategic wealth planning.

PhD routes
For an academic or research-oriented path, relevant areas can include:
A PhD is most useful when the target is research, university teaching, policy, advanced financial research or specialised industry research.

The strongest long-term profile combines investment knowledge + financial planning + technology + client relationships + ethics. AI can increasingly automate portfolio reporting and financial-data analysis, so senior planners should focus on suitability, complex financial decisions, behavioural understanding, client trust and strategic wealth planning.
